text:
rachel: follow-up from today's design sync - proposing a thin Policy Translation Adapter (PTA) between controlplane and runtimes to reconcile tenant policy dialects for Hosted/Dedicated/Private. want quick sanity checks and rollout concerns

 tom: quick summary of goals?

 rachel: goals: 1) let runtimes express enforcement knobs (rate limits, egress whitelist, kms-mode) in a small capability schema; 2) let controlplane continue to author policies in our canonical tenant policy model; 3) PTA translates and validates on bind time and emits audit events

priya: sounds reasonable. big Q: where does enforcement live? translated policy pushed to runtime or enforced by the controlplane proxy?

 diego: my preference is push-to-runtime for Dedicated/Private (for local enforcement) and controlplane-side enforcement for Hosted. avoids double-enforcement but means translation must be symmetric enough

 rachel: agreed. sketch:
1) canonical policy (controlplane)
2) adapter validates -> outputs runtime manifest (opaque fields allowed)
3) runtime returns acceptance + capability warnings
4) controlplane stores a short fingerprint for routing/rollback

example capability schema snippet:
```
- rate_limit: { qps: 20, burst: 40 }
- egress: { allow: ["s3.amazonaws.com"], deny: [] }
- kms: { mode: "customer-managed" }
```

priya: what about mismatches? e.g., canonical says qps 100 but runtime only supports per-minute buckets? adapter should emit a mapping with rationalized values and a warning so tenant can opt-in

tom: yes adapter should produce a delta report. also require tenant opt-in when the delta changes semantics (deny->rate-limit)

diego: SRE note: need an emergency revoke path at runtime for when we need instant kill switch. adapter must include a signed revocation token we can push immediately

ops-bot: checklist: include revocation-token, audit-sink hook, and backoff-policy for repeated translation failures

rachel: rollout plan idea: start with read-only translation mode (generate deltas + telemetry) -> tenant opt-in for translated enforcement -> enable auto-apply for low-risk knobs (rates/egress) -> iterate on kms/auth modes

priya: telemetry: emit translation-diff as structured audit (but obfuscated for secrets). we should tag diffs with translation-version so we can trace when adapter logic changed

tom: tests: unit tests for many-to-one mappings, integration test that binds to a local Dedicated runtime, and chaos test that revokes token mid-traffic to validate revoke path

diego: rollout constraints: for Private deployments we can't assume adapter has network access to runtime control plane. provide a push/pull model: push via controlplane when reachable, and fallback to signed manifests delivered out-of-band for air-gapped installs

rachel: good catch. add both delivery modes: push-over-api and signed-manifest-download. both carry the fingerprint and optional revocation token

priya: security: proof-of-origin for manifests. use short-lived signing keys per-tenant bound at enrollment. rotate keys weekly or on key compromise. record key-id in audit events

ops-bot: policy: require ops signoff for enabling auto-apply on tenant before feature flag flips. include a migration window for existing bindings

tom: UX note: surface the translation-delta in Console and CLI with "why was my QPS reduced" message and link to remediation steps (increase plan or accept mapped limits)

diego: also add a metric for "translation-fallbacks" so PMS can see how many tenants hit mapping friction during rollout

rachel: i'll draft a concise adapter spec and include: schema, signing rules, delivery modes, revoke flow, telemetry fields, and opt-in gating. will share PR link when ready

priya: please include a migration playbook for tenants with custom KMS setups - that will be the trickiest part

ops-bot: reminder: create an ops-runbook with steps: preflight checklist, enable flag, audit verification, revoke steps, and rollback commands

rachel: thanks all 44d i'll iterate on the doc and tag for review. closing this thread for now unless someone has more blockers

priya: none from me, thanks

diego: all good, ping when draft is up
